The house has adequate facilities for Prabhupāda's stay, and the living room is a good place for Prabhupāda to work and relax, with a pleasant vista of the front garden's three tall, thin mango trees and variety of flowers visible through the front windows.

It was standing room only as Prabhupāda held court for twenty minutes to a packed crowd of about fifty devotees and curious locals, we servants settled in quickly, unpacking and setting up his Grundig Dictaphone and other paraphernalia. Prabhupāda has a bedroom with attached bath for his exclusive use; Hansadūta and I are staying in an adjoining room. At the end of his darśana Prabhupāda had me hand out sweets to everyone as they left. He is always meticulous to see that prasādam is distributed whenever he has a meeting, big or small.

\* \* \*

A little later in the morning, Gaurasundara, Pradyumna and family, Pālikā, and other devotees arrived by van from Delhi. They are being housed in nearby Mahajana Dharmashala in Sector 18.

Gaurasundara prabhu gave Prabhupāda his massage again, but now it is Gaurasundara who is feeling a little off-color, whereas I am gaining strength. Because of this, Gaurasundara informed Śrīla Prabhupāda that he would stay only the day and will leave for Delhi and Vṛndāvana tomorrow to complete his business. I'll resume my full duties when he departs.

\* \* \*

Caitya-guru has arranged a five-day *paṇḍala* at nearby Nehru Park in Sector 22. Before the event, this evening's chief guest, the Chief Commissioner of Chandigarh, Mr. T. N. Chaturvedi, came to visit with Prabhupāda at the house. Prabhupāda greeted him warmly, and after a few minutes of convivial discussion they rode to the *paṇḍala* together in the commissioner's car.

The set-up was impressive. Nehru Park is a three-acre patch of open ground in the heart of one of the main markets areas of Chandigarh. Excellent lighting illuminated a colorful canopy extending over and out from a permanent stage, under which an expectant crowd of about twenty-five hundred were gathered for Śrīla Prabhupāda's arrival, ladies on one side and the men on the other. About thirty devotees were already on stage led in an ecstatic *kīrtana* by Hansadūta and Yaśodānandana Swamis, their exuberant dancing and chanting enthralling the audience. When Prabhupāda stepped out of the car and approached the stage, the devotees began to leap high, their big grins and loud, joyous shouts of "Jaya Prabhupāda!" alerting the crowd to his presence. Many rushed forward to offer their *prāṇams* and touch his feet, and we had to form a guard to escort him to the stage. Śrīla Prabhupāda smiled and humbly held his hands together over the handle of his cane in return *praṇāma*, stopping every few feet to allow the spectators to get his blessings.

On stage Prabhupāda was pleased to see a small, decorated altar housing twelve-inch brass Deities of Śrī Śrī Gaura-Nitāi. Next to Them stood a simple but elegant maroon *vyāsāsana*, highlighted with gold braiding, a generous gift from life member Mr. Raj Kumar, the owner of Salwan Furnitures. Flanking the *vyāsāsana* on both sides was a prominent display of Prabhupāda's books.

Prabhupāda approached the Deities and, handing me his cane, got down and offered his obeisances to Their Lordships. Then he took his seat, the devotees sitting on the floor to the left of the stage, his distinguished guests on seats to his right, and Mr. Sethi standing like a faithful sentinel behind his *vyāsāsana*. Pradyumna and I sat by his side, ready to assist.

Chief Commissioner Chaturvedi introduced the program. He has seen our devotees abroad, in airports and doing *kīrtana*, and is greatly impressed with Śrīla Prabhupāda's efforts to spread Vedic culture all over the world. He enthusiastically lauded both Śrīla Prabhupāda personally and his foreign devotees, and urged the crowd to support ISKCON. He took his seat next to Pokar Ram Godara, a local government minister; Murari Lal Bansal, a local business man and the first ISKCON life member in Chandigarh; and Balwant Rai Tayal, MLA for Haryana.

After chanting Jaya Rādhā-Mādhava Prabhupāda launched into a powerful discourse, speaking in Hindi for about fifty minutes to the attentive crowd. His first point was to inform everyone that God is the Supreme Person, possessed of sac cid ānanda-vigraha, a form of eternal knowledge and bliss. Contrasting His transcendental form with our mundane temporary forms that are always subject to distress, Prabhupāda gave a succinct translation of vigraha: "Vigraha means 'manifestation of self.' How can we say the Lord has no form? The Lord is the father of all living beings. I am His son. So if I have form, then how is it possible that my father has no form? He is a person and therefore I am a person." He said that if we could trace our ancestral lines back far enough, we would eventually come to Lord Brahmā, the first living being in the universe. And "above Brahmā there is a supreme father of all."

Sometimes the Lord is described as nirākāra, usually interpreted as "without form," but Śrīla Prabhupāda gave his onlookers a more reasonable understanding. "Now, if someone argues that the Lord doesn't have a form, what kind of argument is that? It is true that you did not see the forefathers of your grandfather and their fathers. Does it mean your forefathers are all nirākāra? Definitely there was a forefather of you, but you did not see him. Then will you say your great grandfather is nirākāra, without form? No! Similarly, the Lord is not nirākāra also.

"In one respect the Lord can be nirākāra, because He doesn't have a form like us. His form is sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha. This is mentioned in scriptures, īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ \[Bs. [5.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/5.1)\]; here Kṛṣṇa is called 'parama', not an ordinary personality."

Anyone who doesn't accept the Lord as the Supreme Person, Prabhupāda said, is, according to scripture, a mūḍhā, no better than an ass. So to save us from making mistakes about the existence of God, he told everyone that we have to read the śāstra, and that this is the special benefit of a birth in India. "If someone wants to know athāto brahma jijñāsā—what is this brahman, what is Bhagavān?—these are all scripture. Why all these scriptures like *Śrīmad Bhāgavatam, Bhagavad-gītā*, Veda, Purāṇa have been written? There are many kinds of scriptures, and these are the treasure of India. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructed, *bhārata bhūmite manuṣya janma haila yāra*: whoever has taken birth in the land of India—this happens due to a huge amount of past pious activities—this is not an ordinary thing. I saw as I traveled all over the world, though at present Indians have fallen down from their original position, that India culture is the highest in the universe. This is my personal experience."

Prabhupāda urged his audience to awaken to the advantage that their birth has given them. Gesturing to the beautiful forms of Śrī Śrī Gaura-Nitāi at his side, he told them, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, bhārata bhūmite haila manuṣya janma yāra janma sārthaka kari' kara para upakāra \[Cc. Ādi [9.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/9.41)\]. This is the mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You can see the vigraha of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. This is His mission. Those who are Indian, those who have taken birth in this holy land of India in human form, not that of an ass, this is the mission for him to make his life successful."

Wherever he travels in India, Prabhupāda repeats the same message again and again, that a birth in this country is a unique opportunity for spiritual advancement and should not be squandered. This paṇḍala was no exception. "Because there are plenty of scriptures named Veda, *Purāṇa, Rāmāyaṇa, Mahābhārata, Bhāgavatam, Bhagavad-gītā*, and so on. Just the Upaniṣads are one hundred and eight in number. Eighteen Purāṇas, *Rāmāyaṇa, Mahā-bhārata, Bhāgavatam*, and *Bhagavad-gītā* are included in those, so one should read all these scriptures scrutinizingly and make one's life successful.

"What is there to learn in this mundane educational system? In one place in *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* it is stated, *kṛṣṇa bhuli' sei jīva anādi bahirmukha* \[Cc. Madhya [20.117](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.117)\]; *ataeva kṛṣṇa veda purāṇa kailā* \[Cc. Madhya [20.122](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/20.122)\] These living entities have forgotten Kṛṣṇa, and when they have forgotten, it is beyond the reach of history; it is anādi. Anādi means before the time of creation—*kṛṣṇa bhuli' sei jīva anādi bahirmukha*—the living entities forgot Kṛṣṇa, the Lord. So the living entities forgot the Lord and hence their remembrance of Kṛṣṇa should be awakened. They should understand that to awaken their remembrance, kṛṣṇa veda purāṇa kailā: Kṛṣṇa has revealed the Veda and Purāṇa for them. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has instructed us, those that have taken their birth in the holy land of India, they should read and listen from the revealed scripture."

Prabhupāda was frank in his assessment of the current condition of his countrymen, yet hopeful that they could still be inspired to follow his example. "In spite of severe downfall, the Indian people still observe different holy festivals and ten thousand or twenty thousand people attend the ceremony. This is in their blood because of taking birth in the holy land of India. They have inclination for devotional service in a part of their existence, and there is a need now to advance it. This is the mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. It is not that only Bhaktivedanta Swami will go abroad and do welfare for others, but you all go abroad. There are plenty of customers of this; everybody will accept with all eagerness."

Pointing out his several dozen mainly Western disciples, Prabhupāda continued, "You see these European and American boys are with me and they are serving me as servants. I didn't bribe them. So why are they with me? They have got something special that they are with me. They are not from a poor country like India that become a sannyāsī and maintain your livelihood simply by begging alms. But they have understood that if there is anything very solid, it is in India. And this is true.

"So Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu teaches us that Indians should learn a lesson of not exploiting those from other countries. No! Para-upakāra! India, you see in the history of the world, never engaged herself to exploit others, but her history is the history of welfare. So bhārata bhūmite manuṣya janma haila yāra janma sārthaka kari' kara para upakāra \[Cc. Ādi [9.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/9.41)\]: you go through all these revealed scriptures and realize them; then only can you be eligible for the welfare of others. When you have nothing, then how can you do welfare for others?"

He informed the audience of the prediction of Lord Caitanya, that His holy names would be spread to every town and village in the world, and told them that this was now being fulfilled. "This is the forecast, and it is happening. You are seeing that we have established 102 centers of ISKCON worldwide. The centers are spread in Europe, America, Australia, in Japan, in Africa, everywhere; no place is left, and everything has been brought into existence single-handedly. Now all of you, making your lives successful, preach this message all over the world. Then you will see how the prestige of India will go higher and higher, and this should be done."

Breaking briefly into English, Prabhupāda's voice boomed forcefully over the loudspeakers: "If you love your country, if you love your culture, you should take up this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement and preach all over the world. That is wanted!" And reverting back into Hindi, he declared, "Yes, that is the mission of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Do you understand it now? My point is that don't neglect it. This is my humble prayer to you. Whether you are a government officer or businessman, you accept this culture, Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and preach. There is no bar to do that."

If there are two main prongs to Prabhupāda's preaching in India, one is trying to arouse people to their spiritual heritage and the other is to defeat impersonalism. The launching of his preaching in Chandigarh was no exception. Explaining that there are two philosophies, one from the Māyāvādīs and the other from the Vaiṣṇavas, he expertly and in short order demolished the impersonal concept and the propaganda that this material world is false. There is no question of anything being false, Śrīla Prabhupāda told everyone, because everything emanates from God. According to śāstra, God is abhijñaḥ. "He knows everything, directly and indirectly—He is God. The rascals they say this is all nonsense . . . because they do not accept the Lord. Those who do not obey God will say this creation is false, but actually this universe, this creation, is not false. The highest technologies have been introduced to run the whole system, and those who have a little bit of intelligence can understand the truth. How the moon is rising; how the tides come in the ocean; the air, earth, fire, sky, water are all assembled together by God-all are false? How is it possible? . . .

"If Brahman is Supreme Truth then how can the Brahman produce something which is false? The 'false' is to say there is no Lord and everything has been created without any cause, automatically—this is false. The intelligent person can appreciate the Lord's presence everywhere analyzing the supreme technologies to create the whole material system. The demon says, 'asatyam': everything is false. We don't say everything is false.

"God Himself is saying that those who claim this material world is false are demons. Why would this material world be false? God Himself is saying, bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva ca, bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā \[Bg. [7.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.4)\]: these fire, ether, water, air, earth, all are My inferior energy. These are My energies; I have created all these things. How is it false? Again He is saying apareyam, the eightfold energy is My inferior energy and there is another prakṛti which is superior to this—*apareyam itas tv anyāṁ prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām* \[Bg. [7.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.5)\], there is another para, superior nature of Mine, jīva bhūtāṁ mahā bāho, that is the living entities. As we are, there is a difference between matter and us. Because we can lord it over matter. We arrange brick, stone, and wood and make a beautiful house with them. So this matter is the energy of the Lord and the jīva is also energy of the Lord, but the living entities are the superior energy."

There was another type of falsity that Prabhupāda condemned as well: the idea that we living beings are the proprietors of this world. "We come to the guesthouse and stay for four days and go away; then should we consider this guesthouse belongs to us? This is illusion. This illusion covers the whole world. Īśāvāsyam idaṁ sarvam \[Īśo mantra [1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/iso/1)\]: everything belongs to God. This is Kṛṣṇa consciousness. One should develop this sense within. To teach this we all together are launching our simple attempt."

Prabhupāda ended his discourse with a final plea. "Our humble request to you all is that this is Indian culture and you should join this. This is not sentimental and not a matter of boasting. Everything here is according to revealed scripture." Drawing attention to the display on either side of him, Prabhupāda told the crowd, "You can see we are presenting eighty-four books of different revealed scriptures to you, so you all please read thoroughly through the scriptures and then accept this movement very seriously. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has said, bhārata bhūmite haila manuṣya janma yāra \[Cc. Ādi [9.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/9.41)\], but we go to Western countries to beg alms. Why should you go there to beg alms? Go there to give something, not for taking something from them. You have the treasure; why should you beg for alms? You have spoiled your treasure and you are going to beg alms from others. This is not good. But this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is noticing that you have wealth, so distribute this wealth to others and make your life successful and do welfare for others. Thank you very much."

With that he opened the floor for questions. Caitya-guru stationed himself at the front of the stage, handing a microphone to the questioners so that everyone could hear their questions as they presented them to Śrīla Prabhupāda. One man came forward and asked, "Has the sac-cid-ānanda a form or not?"

Prabhupāda responded in the affirmative. "Yes. Form. Just like you have got form, asat, acit, nirānanda, He has a form of sac-cid-ānanda."

"But what is it like?" the man asked further.

"When you come to understand, then you will know," Prabhupāda told him. "It cannot be explained in one minute. It requires some education and some understanding. But you have to accept the statement of the śāstra, that vigraha, sac-cid-ānanda. Just like you know that I have got mind, you have got mind. Can you see my mind?"

"No," the man agreed, keen to express his own idea, "but there . . . "

"No, just like you cannot see it but you can perceive. I have got mind; you have got mind. I have got intelligence; you have got intelligence. But what is that intelligence? Can you see it? Something cannot be seen but it can be perceived. Therefore our knowledge is acquired by perceiving. Vedas means śruti. You have to hear and perceive. You cannot see at the present moment; you haven't got the eyes to see."

The man interrupted, wanting to know if surely it wasn't possible to see the sac-cid-ānanda in the light of consciousness.

"Whatever it may be," Prabhupāda told him. "Just like I have already given you the example, that the gross thing you cannot see . . . "

And again the man interrupted, seemingly more interested in his own thoughts than in hearing Śrīla Prabhupāda's. "But the devotee can see the form of sac-cid-ānanda in light of consciousness?"

So Prabhupāda agreed, "Yes, consciousness," and that seemed to satisfy him.

The man's style of questioning and his interruptions prompted Caitya-guru to get up again and inform the crowd that the proper way to approach the spiritual master was through submissive inquiry. At any rate, there were no more questions and we moved into the next part of the program.

Prabhupāda's talk was well received. Even the sound system worked as it should, and he was highly pleased with the whole arrangement. He was enlivened enough that he even stayed on for the slide show of ISKCON's worldwide activities.

At the end, as Prabhupāda dismounted the stage, many in the crowd surged forward to touch his feet. He received their offers of respect and praise graciously, raising his hands in praṇāma as he slowly made his way back to the car. It was ten o'clock by the time we arrived back at the house. Prabhupāda adjudged the paṇḍala a success and praised Caitya-guru for all his hard work.

## October 14th, 1976

Prabhupāda did not translate last night.

At the crack of dawn Śrīla Prabhupāda went for a walk to the Zakir Rose Gardens—a thirty-eight-acre park named after Zakir Hussein, the former president of India. The drive there was pleasant. Chandigarh is a planned city of about 200,000 inhabitants. It is Union Territory and serves as the seat of government for both Haryana and Punjab. There are no skyscrapers, and the roads are clean, wide, and uncongested.

A broad dual carriageway brought us to the main entrance of the park. Stepping out with his small band of followers, Prabhupāda entered through the gate in the thick perimeter hedge and set off along the broad, well-kept walkways. He glanced around in approval as he walked beside a small stream that meandered through the center of the park. Our route took us by a large central pond surrounded by a multitude of flowerbeds, large and small, abounding with over fifteen hundred varieties of fragrant roses. Small clumps of trees, like the willow-like bottlebrush; the towering, orange-blossomed calteria; and many others added to the natural beauty of the area. It is a popular place to walk, and as the day manifest, hundreds of Chandigarh's residents began to appear, nodding politely or offering traditional prāṇama to Śrīla Prabhupāda as they passed us by.

Śrīla Prabhupāda walked slowly for about twenty minutes, but due to weakness, and attracted by the smooth well-kept lawns, he decided to sit for a while. We spread a chaddar out for him, and as soon as he sat down, ten or twenty gentlemen began to gather round. They had either read in the newspapers about his arrival, had attended the program last night, or were simply attracted by the presence of the saintly person in their midst. All were respectful and inquisitive, and a lively fifteen-minute discussion ensued. Prabhupāda was gratified by the interest in his mission and was more than ready to share his knowledge and realizations with the small group of admirers.

He took up the same theme that had dominated his lecture, that Indians were neglecting their real Vedic-based educational systems and therefore losing their spiritual advantage. Even if they read them, he said, they had no understanding.

"Everyone reads *Bhagavad-gītā*, mostly, but they do not understand the first lesson. Dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā, tathā dehāntara prāptiḥ \[Bg. 2.13\]. Nobody understands. What is your understanding about this transmigration of the soul?"

One gentleman took up the discussion while the other dozen listened in with keen interest. "We consider that man gets life after death according to his karma."

Prabhupāda tipped his head to the side in recognition. "Yes." But then he asked, "Do you believe on this?"

"We have this belief," the man replied.

But Prabhupāda wasn't going to let him off so easily. He knew that there is often cursory acknowledgment of the spiritual texts but with little or no application. "Then what is the preparation?" he asked. "If we believe that we have to get another life after death, then what preparation we have made?"

The man hesitated. "Preparation? We . . . The real truth is we don't know." Prabhupāda had immediately exposed the flaw. At least the fellow was honest in his ignorance.

"That is what I am saying," Prabhupāda told him.

The man proffered himself as a student, saying that he would like to know and therefore was approaching learned persons, like Śrīla Prabhupāda.

Prabhupāda reciprocated with the man's humble attitude, and for the next few minutes he impressed the attentive assembly with both his erudition and his realization. He told them that people in general fail to understand that they are fully under the control of material nature; rather, they are thinking themselves independent.

The man agreed that nature was inexorable for all except God. "Does He intervene in our actions?" he asked.

"God interferes if you are a devotee," Prabhupāda told him. "Otherwise, you have to undergo the laws of nature." If a child touchs fire it will still burn even though the child doesn't know it will. Ignorance is no excuse, and we cannot surpass the laws of nature.

"Then what about miracles performed by so many people?" the man asked.

Prabhupāda was immediately dismissive. "That is rascaldom. Nobody can play anything. Magician also can make. It is all foolishness, all rascaldom. They are all rascals and who understands miracle, they are also rascals. Laws of nature cannot be changed."

The man ventured that there may be laws that we don't know about.

Prabhupāda agreed and with a good-humored chuckle told the man, "There are many laws. What do you know? You do not know anything."

The man agreed, thinking that therefore his point was established. "We do not know. Then I say those miracles may be possible according to those laws that we don't know."

But Prabhupāda shook his head, not willing to credit the so-called 'god-man' phenomenon that has so enraptured India's ignorant masses. "There is no miracle. If you touch fire, it will burn; that's all."

Another gentleman submitted a question. "Swamijī, is bhakti mārga enough to have liberation?"

Prabhupāda confirmed that it was but then asked the fellow if he knew what liberation actually was.

"Jīvan mukta," the man replied.

It sounded good, but Prabhupāda probed him more. "No, explain."

Again, when a deeper understanding was called for, the answer was less than satisfactory. The man struggled to identify true liberation. "When feeling one with the consciousness, world consciousness, universal soul."

Śrīla Prabhupāda recognizes impersonalism as the curse of India. As with his lecture last night, he confronted it head on. "Universal soul is spirit, and you are also spirit. In that sense, you are one," he agreed. "But universal soul is different from you. Just like Kṛṣṇa says in the *Bhagavad-gītā* that there are two souls within the body. One soul is the individual soul, and the other soul is the Supersoul. That Supersoul is universal soul, and the individual soul . . . you are individual soul. As soul, the quality is the same, but you are individual soul, and Lord is universal soul. There in the *Bhagavad-gītā* it is stated clearly: *kṣetra kṣetrajña. Kṣetrajña* is the soul; kṣetra is this body. So *kṣetra jñaṁ cāpi māṁ viddhi sarva kṣetreṣu bhārata*: 'I am also *kṣetrajña*, soul, but *sarva kṣetreṣu*.' You individual soul, you know the pleasure, pains, of your body, but you do not know what are the pleasure and pains of my body. Do you know?"

"No, sir," the man agreed while listening closely to follow Prabhupāda's logic.

"Therefore you are individual. You know the pleasure and pains of your body. I know the pleasure and pains of my body. But there is another soul; that is Supersoul. *Sarva kṣetreṣu bhārata*. He knows your pleasure, pains. He knows my pleasure and pains. He knows everyone's pleasure and pains. *Īśvaraḥ sarva bhūtānāṁ hṛd deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati* \[Bg. [18.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.61)\]. Therefore, as soul they are one in quality, but in consciousness they're different. He knows everyone's pleasure and pains; I know my pleasure and pain."

The man appreciated Prabhupāda's point but submitted his question again, this time more specifically. "My humble prayer was that by doing japa, by doing meditation, by doing *bhakti mārga*, need we go to *jñāna mārga* also, or *bhakti mārga* is enough by itself? That was my humble supplication."

Prabhupāda assured him that the path of *bhakti* is enough because it includes everything else. If one has *bhakti* he must also have *jñāna*, and if he doesn't have *jñāna* there is no question of *bhakti*. He explained the exalted position of bhakti. "The *jñāna* is called *brahma bhūta*. That is real *jñāna*. If you understand your position, then it is *jñāna*. If you do not understand your position, then where is jñāna? Do you follow? Therefore Bhagavān says, *brahma bhūtaḥ prasannātmā* \[Bg. [18.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.54)\]. So long you are *ajñāna*, in ignorance, you cannot be happy. But when you are in *jñāna*, then you'll be happy. That is the symptom of becoming *jñānī*. Ātmā becomes very happy. *Na śocati na kāṅkṣati*. He has no more any lamentation and hankering. There are two things in this material world. We are hankering after something which we do not possess, and we are lamenting for something which we possessed and we have lost. This is the disease, material disease. So when one comes to the platform of *jñāna* then he has no more such disease, hankering and lamenting. So *brahma bhūta* means *na śocati na kāṅkṣati* and *samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu*. So long we are on the material platform, we are not samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu. We are thinking, 'You are different from me; I am different from you. My interest is first.' So not *samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu*. But when you become actually *jñānī, brahma bhūtaḥ; samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu, prasannātmā*, then *bhakti* begins. *Mad bhaktiṁ labhate parām*. So *bhakti* is not so easy thing. *Bhakti* means when one understands his real position, means all misunderstanding gone."

What impresses about India is that so many educated persons can quote the *Bhagavad-gītā*—but understanding it is another thing. The man responded agreeably by citing verse 18.66, in which Kṛṣṇa asks for full surrender to Him. "When there is that last śloka in the eighteenth *adhyāya, sarva dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁśaraṇaṁ vraja* . . . "

But of course Prabhupāda was looking for more than dry intellectualism. "How you can do unless you understand your position? When you understand your position, that 'I am eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa,' then you can do that. If I say immediately, 'Mr. Such and such, you give up everything, you surrender unto me,' will you do? No, you'll not do. But when you understand your position—'Yes, it is my duty'—then you'll do it."

The man started to say something about the meaning of *brahma bhūta*, but Prabhupāda interjected, stressing his main point. "*Brahma bhūta* means first of all you understand your identity. You are now identifying yourself as Indian, or as *brāhmaṇa*, or as *kṣatriya*, or white, or black, and so many things."

The man grinned and agreed. "My first identification is my own body."

"Yes, that is *ajñāna*," Prabhupāda told him. "So long you are identifying with the body, you are no better than the animal. So we are doing that. We are fighting. 'I am Indian. You are Englishman. You are this. You are that..' Simply we are fighting, like cats and dogs, they fight. So that is *ajñāna*. How you can be *prasannātmā*? So when one becomes actually situated in spiritual life—*brahma bhūtaḥ prasannātmā*—that is the \[real position\]. In this way, when you make further progress—when you actually understand that you are eternal servant of God—then you surrender. *Bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate* \[Bg. [7.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.19)\]. This situation takes many, many births to cultivate. And when he actually understands, *jñānavān*—not fools, rascals—then *māṁ prapadyate, vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ*. That *mahātmā* is very rare to be found. So *bhakti* is not so easy. *Sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ*. It is not so easy. It takes many, many births to come to the understanding that *vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti*."

Prabhupāda's authoritative command of his subject captivated his audience. They listened carefully, sincerely trying to understand his points and develop their knowledge. The man asked whether the soul experiences the pains and pleasures of each body it occupies as it passes from body to body.

Prabhupāda, encouraged by the response, spoke candidly. "Certainly," he told him. "You just strike one dog—'Ka! Ka! Ka!' Why? Does it not feel pain? And Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose has proved, even the trees, they feel pains and pleasure. It is stage. Just like the tree. If you cut, it does not feel so much pains and pleasure as a human being. It is the development of consciousness. So in human form of body the consciousness is developed. Therefore he can understand what is his position. And therefore for human being there are *śāstras*—the Vedas, the Purāṇas—to understand his position. The tree cannot take advantage of the instruction of *Bhagavad-gītā*. A cat cannot take advantage.

"If we do not take advantage of the opportunity of understanding my identification, then we are committing suicide, jumping like cats and dogs, that's all. Sa eva go kharaḥ. Such persons have been described as go kharaḥ. Go means cows, and khara means ass. Sa eva go kharaḥ—one who identifies \[with\] his body."

Another man who attended the paṇḍala last night joined in. "Mūḍhā, you explained last night."

Prabhupāda's eyes lit up, thankful that his message was getting through and that someone was listening attentively to his discourses. "Yes. This is going on. That's it; that we should take advantage of this human form of life, and know what is our position, why we are in this material world. I am this body or so . . . so many things. This is called brahma jijñāsā. But nobody is interested. That is the effect of bad education. And especially in the Western countries, they do not believe in the next birth. They do not believe, although it is very clearly pointed out by Kṛṣṇa, *dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā* \[Bg. [2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.13)\]: The body is changing from baby body, is coming, becoming a boy, a boy is becoming a young man, young man is becoming middle aged man, and the middle aged man is becoming old man. The body is changing every moment and still they do not believe. Every one of us, we know that we had a childhood body, a boy's body. Where is that body? That body is gone. I am existing, but the body is not existing. Therefore, I have changed body. This simple word, they do not understand. Therefore they are called *mūḍhā*. Kṛṣṇa is pointing out, *dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā, tathā dehāntara prāptiḥ*. Similarly, there is after this, after so called death, the soul changes to another body, and He still further clearly says, *na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre* \[Bg. [2.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.20)\]: 'After the destruction of this body, the person is not killed. He's not dead,' *na jāyate na mriyate vā kadācit*. These things are there, but nobody understands. And they are very good scholar, big, big student of *Bhagavad-gītā*. But these things they do not understand. And they're writing very, very, big, big comments."

When the man responded that everyone believes in transmigration of the soul in theory, Prabhupāda was dismissive. "No. What is that nonsense theory? We must know it actually. What is the use of theory? Theory is no good. You must know factually. That is knowledge. Theory is not knowledge. Anyone can put forward some nonsense theory. That is not knowledge. Knowledge means factual."

And then when the man asked, "How to attain that knowledge then?" Prabhupāda spoke strongly, a hint of admonishment in his tone. "That also Kṛṣṇa is explaining. Why don't you take it? The knowledge is there, but you refuse to accept. So what is fault? Whose fault it is?"

"How should I persuade myself that that . . . ?"

Prabhupāda cut him off, intent on bringing him from the theoretical to the practical. "No. If you don't persuade, nobody can induce you to persuade. If you are obstinate, who can persuade you? You must agree. Therefore it is advised, *tad vijñānārthaṁ sa gurum evābhigacchet, samit pāṇiḥśrotriyaṁ brahma niṣṭham* \[MU [1.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/mundaka/1.2.12)\]; *Tad viddhi praṇi-pāten*a. First of all, you have to surrender. But if you don't surrender, how you'll get knowledge? If you think you are very big man, then how you get knowledge?"

"No, we don't think that we are big men," the man said humbly.

Prabhupāda eased the pressure a bit. "No, no, everyone thinks that, not you. I don't say particular. Everyone thinks, 'I know everything.'"

The man accepted the point, declaring, "We think that we are ignorant, petty creatures. Correct."

"But if you think so," Prabhupāda pressed home, "that you are ignorant petty creatures, then you take knowledge from the authority. Why don't you take it? What is the meaning that you think you are ignorant petty creature, but at the same time, when the most learned person is giving you knowledge, Kṛṣṇa, you don't take it?"

"But there are so many authorities presented to me," the man responded. "There is the Bible, there is the Koran, there is . . . "

Prabhupāda reacted strongly, refusing to accept any excuses for avoiding Kṛṣṇa. "No. First of all, you are born in India. Why you are jumping to Bible?" As the small group burst out laughing, Prabhupāda scolded him. "This is another foolishness. You take care of your own house. You are jumping like monkey to Bible."

The onlookers laughed in delight at his expertise in capturing his quarry, while the man attempted to plead his point. "In our own house there are quite a few dharmas."

But Prabhupāda was already way ahead of him. "Therefore *ācāryavān puruṣo veda*. You have to follow the *ācāryas*. In our country there are *ācāryas*: Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, Viṣṇu Svāmī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu—those who are recognized authority. *Ācāryavān puruṣo veda*. In the *Bhagavad-gītā, ācāryopāsanam*. You have to worship the *ācārya*. The *ācārya's paramparā* is there. *Evaṁ paramparā prāptam imaṁ rājarṣayo viduḥ* \[Bg. [4.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.2)\]."

The man agreed, "There is no dearth of *ācārya* in India." But he again ran aground when he began to list them. "There is Acarya Rajneesh, there is *ācārya* . . . "

Prabhupāda jumped on him again. "No. There is *ācārya*, and there are fools also. *Ācārya* is there, and fools are there also. The agnostics are there. They will not accept any *ācārya*. You accept some *ācārya*, why you become skeptic? At least, we have to accept Kṛṣṇa as the supreme *ācārya*. Why don't you accept Him? If you are embarrassed whom to select *ācārya*, so who can be better *ācārya* than Kṛṣṇa? Why don't you accept Him? That means you want to avoid under some plea. Otherwise there is *ācārya*. If you don't believe in other *ācārya*, you take at least Kṛṣṇa, who is accepted by all the *ācāryas*, either Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, or anyone. Will they not accept Kṛṣṇa as the supreme teacher? Whole world is understanding Kṛṣṇa is the supreme teacher. At least at the present moment they are accepting. We are selling our books daily five to six lakhs' worth, only these Kṛṣṇa consciousness books. And in our country we do not accept Kṛṣṇa as the supreme *ācārya*? What is this? That is our misfortune. Kṛṣṇa is recognized *ācārya*. There is no doubt about it."

Prabhupāda gave a clear definition of the real *ācārya*. "*Ācāryaṁ māṁ vijānīyān nāvamanyeta karhicit* \[SB [11.17.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/17.27)\]. *Ācārya* and Kṛṣṇa are identical. Who is *ācārya*? Who speaks on behalf of Kṛṣṇa, he is *ācārya*. *Ācārya* means one who speaks on behalf of Kṛṣṇa. That is *ācārya*."

The man suggested that the reason we have to follow the writings of the *ācāryas* is because Kṛṣṇa never wrote any books, but Prabhupāda explained that there was no detriment in that. "No, no. Kṛṣṇa did not write, but Kṛṣṇa spoke. If you speak and if I note down and write, what is the difference? Because you did not see, therefore it is not good? He spoke and you note down. Then it is as good. Kṛṣṇa was speaking, and Sañjaya was noting, and that was written by Vyāsadeva in the Mahābhārata. So what is the difference?"

The man's doubts seemed only to increase with whatever Prabhupāda said. "That is one disclosure," he said, indicating that he thought there were other books to be considered. "That is one only, *Bhagavad-gītā*."

And Prabhupāda, as always the perfect *ācārya*, had the answer. "That is sufficient. First of all, you understand few lines of *Bhagavad-gītā*; then jump over other. About this only, one line, *tathā dehāntara prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati* \[Bg. [2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.13)\], if you simply understand this one line, your life will be successful." And so he expertly brought the conversation back to his opening question. "This line, it is clear, that you have to change this body. Have you got any objection to take it?"

"No," the man said.

"Then why you are not serious, 'What kind of body I am going to get?' Here is a body, tree. If you are going to accept a body like this, just how miserable it will be. Why you are not afraid? Just like if you want to go from here, Chandigarh, to Delhi, you have to arrange so many things. So what we are doing, that we have to change this body? And there are 8,400,000 different types of bodies. Which body I am going to get? Why we are not serious? We are spoiling our life."

Prabhupāda's mention of a fixed number of species triggered more speculation in the man's mind. "Those that have become extinct, dinosaurs and those . . . "

And that triggered another strong response from Prabhupāda. "That is rascals' theory. Nothing extinct," he declared to the delight of his other listeners. "Just like \[Darwin\] says that man comes from monkey. Monkey is extinct? Where is the question of extinction? There is no question of extinction. Just like there are first class, second class, third class compartments. If you pay for the first class, you enter into first class. You cannot say that third class is extinct. According to your *karma* . . . *Karmaṇā daiva netreṇa jantur dehopapattaye* \[SB [3.31.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.1)\]. As you pay. If you pay for third class, you enter into third class compartment. If you pay for first class, you enter into first class. So it is according to your *karma* you'll get a body. Why it should be extinct?"

The man wasn't convinced. His empirical training made it difficult for him to accept Prabhupāda's statements. "Because it is extinct. We find there are those . . . fossilized . . . "

"You do not find," Prabhupāda admonished him. "You simply repeat Darwin, that's all. You do not find. You do not see anything. You simply hear from Darwin. You have taken Darwin as your authority. But you don't take authority, Vedas. That is your fault."

"Darwin had drawn that theory from observations."

"Wherefrom he has drawn?" Prabhupāda demanded. "He has speculated only, like a rascal. That's all. Wherefrom he got this thing? He has said that 'It is my speculation.' Speculation is not knowledge. You can speculate in your own way. Knowledge gathered from the authority, that is real knowledge."

With that he decided time was up. His audience were delighted with his strong statements and convictions. Finishing his impromptu darśana, he stood to leave. "Hare Kṛṣṇa," he concluded. As the gathering broke up, at least one of his listeners was sufficiently impressed to inquire about purchasing his books. Prabhupāda told him he could get them at the paṇḍala.

\* \* \*

There was a favorable report on page ten of today's Tribune. Headed with a close-up photo of a smiling and opulently garlanded Śrīla Prabhupāda being received at the airport, the article announced the opening of the five-day *paṇḍala*. It gave a brief description of Prabhupāda's reception and noted that it was his first visit to Chandigarh "after going around the world 16 times." It described Prabhupāda's shaven-headed, dhoti-clad foreign disciples chanting and dancing at the Nehru Park paṇḍala and declared it "easily the most colorful ever held here on the sprawling grounds." It also quoted Caitya-guru prabhu as saying that ISKCON would build a Kṛṣṇa temple in Chandigarh at a cost of ten lakhs and a Kṛṣṇa-Arjuna complex in Kurukṣetra for several crores. Prabhupāda was pleas-ed with the report. Other favorable articles appeared in the Hindi daily Punjab Kesari and several other publications.

\* \* \*

During the morning, Hansadūta Mahārāja read out a stack of mail to Śrīla Prabhupāda and noted down his dictated replies. Mr. Ramkrishna Bajaj, the famous industrialist and the secretary of the Gita Pratisthan (Foundation), wrote to inform Prabhupāda of the revised date for their proposed Gita Prachar conference. The Gita Pratisthan was established on the request of Acarya Vinoba Bhave, a contemporary of M. K. Gandhi, and the upcoming meeting will be the first by a new Coordinating Committee that Śrīla Prabhupāda has been invited to join. Enclosing a list of about twenty-five other invitees, including some well-known Mayāvādīs, Mr. Bajaj gave the dates as December 19th and 20th and the venue as Wardha, Maharashtra. He offered respectful praise of Śrīla Prabhupāda. "As you have made invaluable contribution to the propagation of the message of Gita all over the world, the benefit of your mature advice and guidance will be most helpful in planning the future work of Gita Pratisthan and coordinating the activities of different organizations engaged in this work. We earnestly hope that you will be able to join us in this meeting and shall be grateful if you could kindly let us have your early confirmation in this regard."

Prabhupāda was pleased to accept the invitation. "I will advise Giriraj, my secretary in Bombay to see you in this connection," he replied. "I wish to take with me my sankirtan party, whether you would like to accommodate them. If not then only my personal secretaries, all together five, will go with me, so you have to arrange accommodation for them."

There was also a letter from Girirāja prabhu. Girirāja reported some problems and some successes. It seems that the long reply to the questions from Bhavan's Journal, which Śrīla Prabhupāda first gave in June in New Vrindaban and which Puṣṭa Kṛṣṇa Mahārāja took so long to edit, arrived too late for publication. It was a disappointment, but Girirāja felt that it could still be used elsewhere. "Sadajiwatlal says that he can get it published in ten journals. We are having a lot of preaching engagements and are repeating many of the points in your statement."

He also enclosed a very strongly worded letter written by the son of a prominent *ācārya* in the Vallabha line, which has been circulated to some of our life members. Protesting the article from BTG Vol. 10 #8 in which Śrīla Prabhupāda describes Lord Caitanya's friendly chastisement of Vallabhācārya, the letter condemns ISKCON as a fanatical organization and is very insulting personally to Śrīla Prabhupāda. It calls for our life members to withdraw their support.

Girirāja proposed a solution and requested Śrīla Prabhupāda's advice. "We were thinking of replying to this incident in the 'Hare Krishna Monthly' sent to all of our members every month. The format would be in terms of a letter to the editor stating that 'I was very concerned about the article published in Back to Godhead about Sri Vallabhacarya and I would like you to clarify the situation.' Then we could publish the reply you sent to Smt. Morarjee."

Girirāja's report also had some good news. After holding programs in two important local colleges, the devotees have been invited to teach weekly seminars at Somaiya College and St. Xavier's College. Girirāja said that he was excited about developing the college preaching there, especially to make new Indian devotees. "At both of the engagements mentioned above the students were very enthusiastic to purchase your books. Most of the students wanted to stay and were reluctant to go to their next classes. And some even sneaked out of their next classes to come back and buy your books."

Prabhupāda didn't comment on the Bhavan's Journal episode. He wasn't happy that after so much effort it arrived too late to be used, but he saw that there was nothing to be done. He approved Girirāja prabhu's suggestion for dealing with the agitation against us in Bombay and was very happy to hear about the college preaching. "Your preaching in the colleges is nice," he replied to Girirāja. "Try to make some Indian devotees." He also enclosed a copy of his letter to Ramakrishna Bajaj and asked Girirāja to "do the needful."

A lengthy letter arrived from Dr. Wolf-Rottkay. As a linguist, he tends to get quite verbose in his writing, and this missive was no exception. He is very devoted to Śrīla Prabhupāda, but as a scholar he sometimes struggles with what he regards as naive fundamentalism in our movement. Apart from helping with German language translations, he is trying to help our scientists and is a great friend of Svarūpa Dāmodara prabhu. His letter expressed his difficulty in understanding our preaching approach to modern scientists, and especially our stance on the moon issue. He feels it a contradiction to try to preach through the medium of science while at the same time holding views that contradict the most elementary scientifically based understandings of life and the universe. He said that it was one thing to invite the scientists to be humbly aware of their dependence on God but, "to tell the same professionals to their faces that certain BASICS IN THEIR ACADEMIC BELIEFS which are accepted, as are regular phenomena in nature, all over the 'civilized' world just ARE NOT TRUE, is another thing . . . .

"To deny the Moon and Mars landings and to put the Moon farther way than the Sun while, with Einstein and Max Planck's Constant and the help of all the other modern paraphernalia, very admirably and sophisticatedly (Sadaputa, Svarupa Damodara) refuting the definitely erroneous, yet silently rampant myth of 'science will overcome', namely the troubles of our age and race, - this side by side just will not work. The attempt to 'rock the Galileo-Keplerian Solar System' while using scientific evidence, scientifically and splendidly convincing, in an effort to prove that science is unreliable, fallible (which of course it is) IS A CONTRADICTION IN ITSELF . . . . During a discussion of some astronomical questions with the Department of Astronomy at U.C.L.A. I was, without ANY 'scientific arrogance' told that, for instance, the distance from the Earth to the Moon was known to within fractures of an inch through radar tests. In view of such opinions I must deem it hopeless that speaking to the 'scientists' can bear fruit. Frantic attempts to support the Vedic statements about the Moon by speaking of faked landings ('there are enough deserts around in California and Arizona'-'opinions' heard many times at the Los Angeles and Atlanta temples) may, however become as politically dangerous as the earlier mentioned 'Hitler myths' which persistently stick in the minds of the young, uninformed prabhus and are sprung on me as the unfortunate victim and sufferer again and again when my being a German is mentioned during talks. I do not know what to think of such things really.

"Please be advised, beloved Master, by one who in devotion, but also IN DEEP CONCERN, feels called upon to speak up and out as an appointed council. As in other matters which I brought to the Master's knowledge, I also here see a danger that should be neutralized as quickly as possible.

"In reverence and gratitude, W.H. Wolf-Rottkay, disciple."

Dr. Wolf-Rottkay also enclosed a prayer and a short appreciation of the Brahmā-saṁhitā, Prabhupāda's presentation of which, he said, often fills his best devotional hours.

Prabhupāda smiled when he heard the contents. He has had many discussions with Dr. Wolf-Rottkay, his sage advice helping the good doctor to stave off serious conflicts in the juxtaposition of his transcendental heart and his mundane mind.

Prabhupāda wrote back, "Regarding the scientists, we have entrusted our own three scientists, namely Swarup Damodar, Sadaputa, and Madhava, and we leave the matter to them; we do not say anything ourselves, but are leaving it to them. But there are many common men who do not believe that they have gone to the moon planet. So as common men we can simply say, how can dust and rocks reFlect so much of light as to illuminate the night, like the sun at day. It is simply bogus to say that the moon is full of dust and rocks. \[That\] such a beautiful soothing planet is full of dust and rocks with no living beings there is simply unbelievable. You are a learned scholar, do you think it is believable that dust and rocks can illuminate the whole universe at night? It is so soothing and beautiful. I shall be very glad to receive further enlightenment in this connection from your good self."

From Jaśomatīnandana dāsa in Gujarat, Prabhupāda received a report on the farm that Mr. Bhogilal Patel is proposing to donate to us. There are some government formalities to satisfy, which will take a few weeks to arrange. Consisting of one hundred and eight acres of rich alluvial soil, it is worth between eight and ten lakhs. According to the manager of the farm, crops worth three lakhs a year can be grown with little effort or investment. The manager described the land as "a piece of gold." It is also ideally located, only five miles from the city of Ahmedabad. Jaśomatīnandana invited Śrīla Prabhupāda to visit if his health permits.

Apart from this, Jaśo is struggling, as he and his wife are now there alone. An American couple who were helping have returned due to visa expiration, and yet he is still printing a monthly magazine, *Bhagavad-gītā*, and other small books in Gujarati, as well as making life members, preaching, and handling all the managerial affairs. He feels that if the farm is obtained, he will need some help and suggested that some of the men at the Vṛndāvana temple could be sent. Finally, he requested permission to install Gaura-Nitāi Deities on Govardhana-pūjā on the 24th of this month in order to make everything "nice and auspicious."

Śrīla Prabhupāda is eager for the farm projects to develop. He wrote back suggesting how the land can best be utilized for our purposes. "You say the farm is only five miles from the city, so we will build our temple on that land. The farmers should be trained up to become devotees of Krishna. The same idea I have already given for Hyderabad farm. Invite the local farmers to participate in Kirtan and prasadam distribution, engage them to work the land. They may keep whatever they require for their maintenance, and the excess production may be traded or sold. But we are not going to develop a competitive farming enterprise for making money. The basic principle is to become independent of artificial city life, working in factories producing nut and bolts. Gandhi had this idea, the one defect was that there was no Krishna in the center. So the same idea of village organization, but keeping Krishna in the center should be introduced on our farm projects."

In view of his lack of manpower, Prabhupāda advised Jaśo not to install Deities there until there are enough devotees to take proper care of Them. And in this regard he told him, "Regarding men, everywhere there is shortage, we cannot continue to import men continually."

\* \* \*

I am now fully fit and have resumed my duties as masseur. Gaurasundara prabhu, who himself is still feeling a little ill, returned to Delhi this morning after taking his leave of Śrīla Prabhupāda. After so many years away, by some special mercy, he has again been engaged in intimate service to his spiritual master, Kṛṣṇa's pure devotee. Prabhupāda was pleased with his service and gave him his blessings and encouragement.

\* \* \*

There were no special visitors during the day, but Śrīla Prabhupāda held a general darśana in the late afternoon, which was well attended. At 6:30 he was met at the house by tonight's chief guest, Shri Hansraj Sharma, the Finance Minister of Punjab. He was accompanied by Mr. SP Vohra, the town planner for Haryana. They talked for a few minutes, and Śrīla Prabhupāda presented him with a copy of one of the volumes of the *Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā*. Then they drove together to the paṇḍala.

Again there was a big crowd, even larger than the first night, perhaps due to the news articles this morning and also the arrangements of Caitya-guru prabhu. He and the devotees have been going out during the night, sticking up large, beautiful posters all around the city advertising the *paṇḍala*. He has also arranged for large banners to hang across the main roads, welcoming Śrīla Prabhupāda and giving the dates and times for the programs. Devotees have also been going out during the day, performing *nagara-saṅkīrtana* for the first time in the streets of Chandigarh, much to the delight and interest of the residents, most of whom have never seen Western boys in the traditional garb of Vaiṣṇavas. When people inquire about Śrīla Prabhupāda and ISKCON, the devotees direct them to the paṇḍala.

As Śrīla Prabhupāda and his guests mounted the stage, the devotees, led by Hansadūta Swami, intensified their chanting, dancing and singing with great energy and enthusiasm. Prabhupāda offered his obeisances to the Deities and then took his place on the vyāsāsana. After the devotees completed their kīrtana, Mr. Sharma gave a short message of appreciation for Śrīla Prabhupāda and his ISKCON mission, but due to a prior commitment he took his leave early, promising to come again before the completion of the paṇḍala programs.

Unfortunately, it wasn't a good night for me. I made a stupid blunder. After His Divine Grace had taken his seat and was about to start his lecture, I reached into my cloth shoulderbag, handed him his *karatālas* and placed the *Bhagavad-gītā* on its stand. At the end of his chanting of Jaya Rādhā-Mādhava, he sat facing his expectant audience, waiting for me to hand him his reading glasses so that he could begin his lecture. But when I reached into the bag for them, the glasses were not there. In great apprehension, I had to lean forward and inform Prabhupāda that I had forgotten them.

With no trace of emotion, still facing the audience, his expression unchanging and giving me not so much as a glance, Prabhupāda said quite simply, "Then why have you come?"

Knowing full well that it was a totally futile effort but not wanting to be guilty of not making at least some attempt to rectify my mistake, I ran off the stage, jumped into the car, and raced back to the house to retrieve the glasses. Of course, when I returned Prabhupāda was already well into his lecture and it was too late. Typically, he didn't mention the incident afterwards.

Prabhupāda spoke in Hindi again for about fifty minutes, centering his talk on the contrast between the two kinds of natures—the divine and the demonic—and the responsibility we have as human beings to choose between them. To be a demon or a demigod is not a question of birth, he said. "Demigods take birth in the families of demons, and demons also take birth in the families of demigods. Now in this Kali yuga, the number of demons are more. In Satya-yuga everybody is a demigod. In Tretā yuga three parts are demigods and one part is demoniac. In Dvāpara yuga half the number is demigod population and other half is demoniac. In Kali-yuga three parts are demons and one part is demigod. And as it advances, the demons will be more."

To make it perfectly clear what he meant by demon, Prabhupāda had Pradyumna prabhu read out verse [16.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/16.7). "What is their nature, what is their identification, the Lord Himself describes them in *Bhagavad-gītā*. So the first quality is *pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca janā na vidur āsurāḥ*; these people do not know the purpose of their life. They cannot understand. Just eat, drink, and make merry. What else do they know? Big, big professors in Europe, especially in Moscow, they say that after death there is nothing, there is no life after death-this is *āsuric* mentality. If you say there is a next life according to one's karma, then it becomes difficult for them, because they perform only sinful activities. Although it is actually true, they do not want to believe in next life.

"This is all Vedic knowledge—transmigration of the soul, leaving the present body to accept another body according one's karma. *Karmaṇā daiva netreṇa* \[SB. [3.31.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.1)\]. What the next body will be after death is decided by daiva netreṇa, superior supervision. Thus he gets a different body, as long as the body fits, and depending upon what kind of body he wants, he has to stay in that body. The scriptures give the example of how we walk. We place our first foot and then when we see where to put the next, we take the next step; similarly, we live in this body and as soon as this body becomes unfit, whatever body we are going to get next, immediately we enter that other body. So Kṛṣṇa says *na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre* \[Bg. [2.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.20)\]; don't think that after this body is dead, everything is finished.

"The atheists say, 'After burning the dead body, what else remains? What is all this "good and bad activities"? After the body is burnt everything is finished.' There are so many atheists in our country who are gone. One is Cārvāka; his saying is that 'As long as you have body, enjoy; *ṛṇaṁ kṛtvā ghṛtaṁ pibet*.' In our country India it is thought that if you eat palatable dishes made of ghee then you enjoy the most. Like in Europe and America, they eat meat, especially beef. They think that is enjoyment. But in India, people eat dishes made with ghee, so he instructs, ṛṇaṁ kṛtvā ghṛtaṁ pibet. 'If you think, "We don't have money; how are we going to get ghee?" just borrow and if you are not able to return, and if you think it is sin and it is not proper, *bhasmī bhūtasya dehasya kutaḥ punar āgamano bhavet*—why are you worried about this? Once this body dies and is burnt, there is no rebirth; everything finished at death.' Atheist! But the Lord Himself is speaking, so we have to take knowledge from that. What is the use of taking knowledge from the foolish people?"

Prabhupāda described the four qualities of the foolish-bhrama (the tendency to commit mistakes), *pramāda* (the tendency to be illusioned), *vipralipsā* (the tendency to cheat), *karaṇāpāṭava* (imperfect senses—and declared that therefore, because our present understanding is conditioned, real knowledge is acquired, especially in India, from the Vedas. He noted that, unfortunately, the path of the *śāstras* is not acceptable to many; they prefer to live like atheists. "Therefore the symptoms of Kali-yuga are '*mandāḥ sumanda matayo manda bhāgyā hy upadrutāḥ* \[SB [1.1.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.10)\]. Mostly the people are unfortunate; there are no fortunate people. You see these Americans. They do not know what poverty is. There are no poor people there. They have taken birth in that place and thus they are leading life like that. They have food to eat, place to sleep, but they are *manda bhāgyā*—birth in the good place, good nation, but they are unfortunate."

As far as upadravas, or disturbances go, he said that there are many and recalled how in England in the summer they had to import water because of drought. "There are different upadravas: adhyātmika, adhidaivika, and adhibautika. Here there is suffering. In Kali-yuga the suffering keeps increasing. The demons do not know how to intelligently lead life. Eat, drink, and enjoy-this theory, this kind of philosophy is the problem. Therefore the scriptures challenge it. There are so many problems, so what is the reason? Pig's life. And what is this pig's life? Work hard whole day, search where the stool is, eat and enjoy, and wherever there is dirt and stink, take rest. This is not life. No, this is not human life."

Citing Lord Ṛṣabhadeva's teachings, Prabhupāda told everyone that human life is actually meant for performing austerities. Austerity, he announced, helps in every way. A rich man also needs to perform austerity; otherwise he won't obtain his riches. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa informs us that within this body we have another body, a cit-body, the spiritual soul. By austerity we purify this eternal body. If we don't, we face repeated birth and death. This is the position of the demons. "*Pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca*. They don't have the intelligence to think that we are again and again taking birth and how to stop this . . . The Vedic knowledge gives instructions so that we don't have to take birth in another body and we can stay as the eternal spirit soul. This stops birth, death, old age, and disease. This is the purpose of life. This type of life—eating, drinking, and enjoying—is the path of *pravṛtti*. And *nivṛtti-marg* means stopping this and acting so as to get the complete *cit-*body, spiritual body, and go back to the Lord and be active and play with Him. We can get this type of body."

Prabhupāda stated emphatically that when God comes, He shows us that His activities are not mundane but pure and transcendental, and that the purpose of performing austerity is to understand this. *Tapo-divyaṁ* means that in order to obtain something higher we have to give some things up, and therefore in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, four regulations are taught.

Singling out no illicit sex as an example, Prabhupāda said that this means having sex only with one's wife. He quoted Cāṇakya Paṇḍita, saying that the brahmacārī is taught to see all women as his mother. This was the training of the *varṇāśrama* system. "Now this is all given up. By giving up, it has fallen down. We have to surely make efforts to bring it up. But we are unfortunate; we are not trying. We have *śāstra*. There are instructions, the Lord Himself is saying c*ātur varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa karma-vibhāgaśaḥ* \[Bg. [4.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.13)\]; these four *varnas* are all made by God's rules for the purification of the soul. We have to accept this, but the demons do not know; *pravṛttiṁ ca nivṛttiṁ ca na vidur āsurāḥ janāḥ*. They do not accept this, but it is there."

Prabhupāda said that everything meant for understanding God is given in *Bhagavad-gītā*, which is the essence of all the Vedic literatures. Until we come to that point, he asked, "what is the use of your Vedic study?" Because people are particularly foolish in Kali-yuga, Kṛṣṇa therefore appeared at the beginning of it five thousand years ago and taught *Bhagavad-gītā* to Arjuna, especially to benefit the people of this age. "So that is still available. We have to take knowledge from this and practice in our own lives, and only then our Indian culture will be safe. But if we give all this up and wander around just for sense gratification, we will be lost. So the scripture says, tapo divyaṁ: this is proper. If in this human form of life we don't do tapasya, then it is like Cārvāka Muni says: *ṛṇaṁ kṛtvā ghṛtaṁ pibet yāvaj jīvet sukhaṁ jīvet*, this is all there, symptoms. *Na śaucaṁ nāpi cācāro*: they are not clean. Until now in Bhārata *varṣa*, we have seen in the villages, there are poor people—even in Bombay we have seen poor people—they go bathe in the ocean early every morning. But the so-called educated, advanced, big people—they don't take bath; they don't bathe for seven days. These people don't have facility for taking bath at home, so once in a week they pay and take bath in the bathrooms in the marketplace. This is the symptom of a demon. No cleanliness. *Na satyaṁ teṣu vidyate*, even the behavior is not good. No character; saying the truth is like a laughing story. One who says more lies is very clever. You can see in the courts: one who tells more lies becomes the winner."

Due to these conditions, therefore, Kṛṣṇa comes Himself to declare that He certainly exists. He is the source of everything, but to understand this is no ordinary thing. Prabhupāda said that it takes thousands of lifetimes of discussion for those with knowledge to finally understand that Vāsudeva is everything. Therefore Kṛṣṇa comes Himself. Prabhupāda surveyed the several thousand attentive souls arrayed before him under the glare of the paṇḍala lights and urged them to accept *Bhagavad-gītā* as it is. "It is not that 'We take whatever we want by adding or subtracting from Your words.' No, this is not how *Gītā* reading is done. One has to accept whatever the *Gītāśāstra* says. Everything has to be accepted. 'Whatever You have said has to be accepted,' sarvam etad ṛtaṁ manye \[Bg. [10.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.14)\]. This is the result of understanding *Gītā*. If somebody has really understood *Gītā*, it means he has accepted whatever is in the *Gītā*, that is, 'Whatever You have said.'"

He condemned the over-intelligent who change Kṛṣṇa's message to suit their own ideas. "*Ardha kukkuṭī nyāya*, the clever people do this. There is one example. A person was rearing hens. The hen was giving eggs every day. So this man thought that 'This hen gives eggs daily, but I have also to feed it everyday, but the egg comes only from the back, so let me cut off its mouth so that I don't have feed the mouth and save money.' This fool does not know that if you don't feed it through the mouth, egg cannot be given. This is called *ardha kukkuṭī nyāy*a. There are some foolish people like this who cut the *Gītā*, here, there, like whatever comes to their mind and learning a few verses becomes a big scholar. He is not a proper student of *Gītā*, as he thinks himself to be; he is cheater. If you just accept *Gītā* as it is, as the Lord has said, you are suffering so much here, giving up God. Accept God, then everything will auspicious. If you just read *Gītā* and practice as given in *Gītā*, there won't be any kind of problem for you."

Prabhupāda made it a point to say that accepting Kṛṣṇa's guidance does not mean becoming inactive. As he did in Aligarh a few days ago, he used the examples of Arjuna and Hanumān to demonstrate that the devotees act powerfully on the Lord's behalf. "It is not that 'Now I have become a devotee of the Lord, I don't have anything to do. I will just simply sit.' No, this is not what the Lord is saying. The Lord taught *Bhagavad-gītā* to Arjuna and told him to fight. He did not say, 'Now you stop fighting and run away from the battlefield.' Arjuna did not want to fight but wanted to be nonviolent and be secure: 'Oh Kṛṣṇa what is the use of this fighting. In reality they are our brothers; let's stop and enjoy the kingdom.' But the Lord said, 'No, you fight.' The Lord does not say, 'You become My devotee and simply sit.' No. We see in our Bhārata varṣa there were fights. There was fight between Rāma and Rāvaṇa and fight between Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas. But the heroes are Vaiṣṇavas, Hanumānjī and Arjuna. If you become a Vaiṣṇava it is not that you just have to simply sit and be lazy. No. For the Lord's sake we should do everything. This is Vaiṣṇava. *Ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānu śīlanaṁ* \[Brs. [1.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/rupa-brs1/1.1.11)\]. Do whatever the Lord says."

Once again Prabhupāda's talk was well received and there were plenty of questions. This time, though, Caitya-guru announced each one over the microphone and then Prabhupāda replied. A man asked what type of transformation took place when Kṛṣṇa spoke the *Bhagavad-gītā*.

Prabhupāda answered with clarity and conviction. For him, there is no mystery in the *Gītā*: "After hearing, Arjuna said *kariṣye vacanaṁ tava* \[Bg. [18.73](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.73)\] and before, he was saying *na kariṣye vacanaṁ tava*. So the Lord chastised him. He said to Arjuna, 'Why are you behaving like a child coming on the battlefield? This behavior of yours is not at all according to ethics. He said, *anārya juṣṭam* \[Bg. [2.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.2)\]—this is not at all like an *ārya*, a knowledgeable person; rather it is like an *anārya*, an uncivilized one. 'You are well known as My friend and you came here to fight, and you are such a rascal that you are trying to escape!' This was the mood of Arjuna—the Lord is ordering him to fight and Arjuna was replying *na kariṣye vacanaṁ tava*: 'I will not obey You.' When that same Arjuna heard *Bhagavad-gītā* very thoroughly, he decided, *kariṣye vacanaṁ tava*. This prefix 'na' has been removed now. He is saying, 'I must do whatever You say.' This is the main change, and it is very easy to understand. If one's decision has been turned to *kariṣye vacanaṁ tava* after reading *Bhagavad-gītā*, then his reading of *Bhagavad-gītā* is successful. Otherwise he will remain a rascal—*na mām duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ* \[Bg. [7.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.15)\] So everybody should acquire enough intelligence by reading *Bhagavad-gītā* and declare *kariṣye vacanaṁ tava—*'I must do what Lord Kṛṣṇa has said,' that's all."

The next man stepped up to the microphone and asked, "You discussed earlier that the way of asking questions to the guru is *tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā* \[Bg. [4.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.34)\] offering him humble obeisance, etc. You said that even though you may be knowledgeable you should not show that attitude in front of guru. Please explain that."

"One who preaches that which is said by the Lord is a guru," Prabhupāda responded. "The Lord has given definition of *dharma* as *sarva dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁśaraṇaṁ vraja*. So the duty of the guru is to direct the living entities to the contemplation of the lotus feet of the Lord. That person is the guru; others are cheaters. One who considers himself as Kṛṣṇa is simply a cheater. And one who says, 'Take shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa,' he is guru. That is, you should judge him by what he says. If the guru says that you take shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa because Kṛṣṇa says *mām ekaṁśaraṇaṁ vraja*, then he is actually guru. And one who speculates, he is not guru. This is the point you should judge on, that's all."

The third question was a little speculative. "In the Rāmāyaṇa it is said that Lord Rāma fought a battle against Rāvaṇa, and in the Mahābhārata the battle was fought in the presence of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord. So what about the third war? Who will fight that?"

Prabhupāda's quick reply made the audience laugh. "You are to fight the third war! Why you are thinking in advance for the third war? First of all you accept the instructions of the Lord given in the second one; then there may be some scope to think about the third one. Lord is instructing, *sarva dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁśaraṇaṁ vraja*, so follow it. Then you will understand the third one. Yes!

"There is a third avatāra, and that is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He instructs, *harer nāma harer nāma harer nāmaiva kevalam kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva nāsty eva gatir anyathā.* Actually, this is not directly spoken by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, but it is quoted from *Bṛhan nāradīya Purāṇa.* This *harer nāma harer nāma harer* is meant especially for this age of Kali, so do it! This will create good for others, and you will be freed from the three modes of material nature and be happy."

The final questioner asked about one of the popular figures on the current spiritual circuit. "Śrī Sai Baba is the Lord Himself-what is your opinion of this?"

Perhaps the questioner was hoping for a controversial reaction, but Śrīla Prabhupāda rarely criticizes other so-called gurus in public. Nevertheless, by his reply the audience understood what he really thinks, and they were delighted. "We are rascals, so we do not know all these things," he said, taking the humble stance. "We know only that Kṛṣṇa is the Lord. We are not very scholarly." The audience laughed in appreciation at his punch line: "We only know *kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam* \[SB [1.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.28)\]—only Kṛṣṇa is the Lord and the rest are all cheaters."

In accordance with Śrīla Prabhupāda's standards, Caitya-guru has arranged for the distribution of prasādam when Prabhupāda leaves the paṇḍala. Puri, halava, and fruit, along with caraṇāmṛta, is distributed from the stage. Śrīla Prabhupāda told him to offer it to Śrī Śrī Gaura-Nitāi in full view of the public just to show them how we offer our food before eating.

## October 15th, 1976

Due to the strain of the *paṇḍala* program and his own weak health, Śrīla Prabhupāda has not translated since we have been here. He is requiring more rest.

For his walk, Prabhupāda went once more to the Rose Garden and again spent a substantial part of his outing sitting on the lawns. His presence in the city has been noted, and many gentlemen acknowledged him and paid their respects as they passed by on their daily exercise. Once again, a small group gathered around him on the grass and Prabhupāda gave another impromptu *darśana*, engaging in a sometimes-lively debate about the purpose of human life. One fellow in particular expressed his opinion that beyond eating and sleeping and maintaining his family, there is nothing more. He had no time or interest for God. Śrīla Prabhupāda presented a strong case for spiritual development, but although the man could not deny its validity, neither could he readily accept it.

On the drive back to the house, Śrīla Prabhupāda expressed his regret that society in India has come to such a stage. But he is not surprised. People are turning their backs on their own culture to run after the West, and decades of secularism in government and education have significantly undermined the natural spiritual inclinations of the *Bhārata-vāsīs*. Vedic knowledge and outlook have been eroded and devalued to the point of inconsequence in the lives of the majority, especially in the cities. Clearly, His Divine Grace's work is as keenly needed here as it is in the West.

\* \* \*

Hansadūta Swami came with more mail during Śrīla Prabhupāda's massage, and as His Divine Grace allowed me to squeeze, press, and rub his body, he heard the letters and gave his replies.

Cittahārī dāsa, the president of our Auckland temple, wrote regarding Śrīla Prabhupāda's suggestion, made in response to his previous inquiry last month that he deposit thirty thousand dollars he had received into the Māyāpur-Vṛndāvana Trust account in Los Angeles. Cittahārī expressed his reluctance to do this. "When I first came here as president three months ago there were debts of $45,000 owed by the Society brought about by mismanagement in both ISKCON and Spiritual Sky over the last three years. With the permission of Guru Kṛipa Swami and Rsabdeva das in Los Angeles I have negotiated the sale of Spiritual Sky which was a financial liability and a drain on our preaching, temple, resources and men.

"Due to this sale the financial situation has been eased a little but we are still in a position where our Temple is in danger of being sold to pay off the mortgage. Apart from this we have a large outstanding debt to your Bookfund. So I am begging your permission Srila Prabhupada to use the money in the service of Sri Sri Radha Giridhari here in Auckland and any excess I will send to Los Angeles as you have suggested."

Prabhupāda was sympathetic to both the situation and the fact that the money in question came from Cittahārī's personal funds. He told him, "It is your money, so you can do with it whatever you like. If you feel the money is needed there, then use it accordingly. I have no objection."

Kīrtanānanda Swami sent an inquiry about a new film the BBT is making, intended for training devotees in the art of book distribution. According to Kīrtanānanda the film shows a questionable method of collecting money, which may in fact be illegal. He feels that the film will be a danger to ISKCON and might be used as incriminating evidence if ever a court case is brought against us. Noting that his zone is probably number one in terms of books distributed per devotee, he said, "I simply want to know what You want and then I will be satisfied no matter the result. I might add that this technique is never used in this zone nor is the other technique of using lies, i.e. feeding starving children, collecting for VFW, etc., and we maintain a high standard. Why should we jeopardize the future of this movement on some questionable means that is not necessary? We say, 'Purity is the force,' then why is tricking necessary? This matter was supposedly resolved at Mayapura a year ago, but it seems that only a clear and unequivocal statement from Yourself can ease everyone's mind. Please forgive me for bringing this matter before You."

Kīrtanānanda Mahārāja also enclosed a check, in the hope that it would "ease Your headache," and added that the Palace they are building is attracting many visitors and should be ready for Śrīla Prabhupāda by next spring.
